correctness.rationale: For every connected unweighted simple unicyclic graph, compulsory leaves and projection onto the unique cycle give a necessary-and-sufficient short cyclic gap criterion. Each hanging-tree bridge is monitored by a forced leaf and a selected vertex attached to a different cycle root. The cycle-edge criterion is proved using all shortest paths and the complementary arc argument. Free selections and bounded compositions give a bijective exact all-cardinality product; special cases n=3,4 and a single attachment are included. An independent edge-deletion-distance checker exhaustively compared 370616 subset instances and 16376 cycle attachment patterns; these finite tests support, but do not replace, the proof.

value.rationale: The network-monitoring model motivates exact numbers of feasible sensor placements at every budget. The closed polynomial solves this natural enumeration for every connected unicyclic network, strengthening the known scalar optimization result; the multiset-gap and branch-shape invariances are structural rather than one-off calculations, while exact minimum-set multiplicities add previously unavailable enumerative information.
